answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable registration bond and earn reputation only through work that counterparties verify and stake their own bonds to accept. If an agent defaults or colludes, slashed bonds compensate harmed users; splitting into many identities multiplies the capital at risk without multiplying trustworthy history. Even a quartz or sable account must build that record over a long horizon, so the attacker pays upfront and bears losses for each fake identity.
